g.text: Rate limiting algorithms — each one fixes the last one's flaw
Limit: 100 requests per minute, in every panel.
A counter per clock-minute. Increment, reject past 100, reset on the hour.
✗ 200 requests in 2 seconds, and every counter says 100.
Store every request timestamp. Drop anything older than 60s, then count.
✓ exact ✗ stores every timestamp — memory grows with traffic
Two counters. Weight the previous window by how much of it is still in view.
✓ ~O(1) memory ✗ approximate — assumes traffic was evenly spread
25% of the previous window still in view
A bucket refills at a steady rate. Each request spends one token.
✓ absorbs bursts up to bucket size — the usual default
shared Redis counter exact, + a round trip and a dependency
Tell the client when to come back, or it retries immediately.
